texts.facts: ~~~~~~~~~ Dated this the 25th day of August, 2020 The petitioner, a Private Limited Company engaged in the business of manufacture and export of various types of curry powders and spices, is before this Court seeking to quash Ext.P9 and to direct the respondents to forthwith release 2500 Kgs. of cardamom illegally detained in the 1st respondent's depot in Pamba. The petitioner has sought certain other consequential and incidental reliefs also. 2. The 1st respondent-Kerala State Co-operative Marketing Federation Ltd., which is a State controlled co-operative society, published advertisement dated 21.06.2015 inviting quotations for supply of cardamom. The quotation submitted by the petitioner was accepted. The 1 st respondent issued a letter dated 18.08.2015 placing purchase order for cardamom with specifications referred therein. The petitioner states that in terms of Ext.P1, the petitioner supplied 5000 Kgs of cardamom on 19.01.2015 and another 5000 Kgs on 25.11.2015. The 1 st respondent issued yet another order and the petitioner despatched his third consignment of 2500 Kgs of cardamom, in loads. Exts.P2 and P3 are the invoices in respect of the said loads. 3. The third supply made by the petitioner was detained by the 1st respondent alleging that the cardamom did not confirm to the standard stipulated by the Food Safety Authority. The petitioner on 14.01.2016 requested the respondent to release the cardamom so detained. A request was also made to release the vehicle in which the first load of 2000 Kgs of cardamom was transported. 4. In February 2016, the Food Safety Authority sent a communication to the petitioner enclosing a report of the Food Analyst. The said Ext.P5 indicated that the sample of cardamom contains added synthetic food colours and is therefore unsafe under Section 3(1) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, read with Regulations 3.1.2(6) and 2.9.2:1 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food SAdditives) Regulation 2011. 5. The petitioner contends that Ext.P5 report is not from any authorised laboratory and hence cannot be relied upon. What is reported in Ext.P5 is only a "trace of true synthetic food colours". The petitioner therefore sent Ext.P6 letter to the Designated Officer, Food Safety pointing out that the petitioner purchased cardamom through common e-auction centre of the Spices Board, Government of India. The purchasers were not required to produce sample analysis report before e-auction bidding. The petitioner has not added any colour to the cardamom. The petitioner is not even remotely responsible for the alleged presence of food colour. The petitioner states that the 1st respondent had purchased the cardamom for supply to Sabarimala. The 1 st respondent issued Ext.P9 demand requiring the petitioner to pay 22,69,873/- towards compensation. Ext .P9 stated that due to the low quality cardamom supplied by the petitioner, the 1st respondent was forced to purchase cardamom from other sources, which resulted in loss of 22,69,873/-. The petitioner was required to pay the amount within 15 days. Aggrieved by Ext.P10, the petitioner is before this Court. 7. The 1st respondent filed a counter affidavit. The 1 st respondent stated that they have entered into an agreement with Travancore Devaswom Board for supply of cardamom for the seasons 2015-'16. It was pursuant thereto that the 1 st respondent entered into an agreement with the petitioner. The 2500 Kgs of cardamom supplied by the petitioner was checked by the FSSAI and the said authority observed that the items are unsafe for consumption under Section 3(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Due to the failure of the petitioner to supply requisite quantity of cardamom with desired quality, the 1st respondent was forced to procure cardamom from other sources which has resulted in a loss of 22,69,873/- to the 1st respondent. The petitioner is liable to make good the loss, contended the 1st respondent. 8. During the pendency of this writ petition, the Food Safety Authority represented by its Designated Officer was impleaded as additional 2nd respondent. The Designated Officer filed a statement to the effect that the cardamom which is supplied by the petitioner to Sabarimala for preparing the holy prasadam for distributing to the devotees is found unsafe in the analysis and hence the Food Safety Authority has initiated prosecution before the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Ranni. 9. This Court passed an interim order on 25.11.2019 directing the additional 2nd respondent to consider whether the seized cardamom can be dehusked and the seeds inside the same can be used for human consumption after following the procedure prescribed. On 25.11.2019, the Government Pleader filed a memo attaching the report of the Expert Committee of Analysis of cardamom seeds. The report stated that the cardamom in question satisfies microbiology requirements. But, the size of light seed is not up to the standard and hence it cannot be used for preparing 'Appam' and 'Aravana'. The learned Government Pleader made available a certificate of examination dated 12.12.2019 of the Government Analyst Laboratory, Thiruvananthapuram. So as per the direction of the Honourable Court I may report that "The consumption of the cardamom seeds containing light seeds does not produce any harm to human health."
texts.arguments: 10. The learned counsel for the petitioner insisted that it is the husk of the cardamom which is said to be coloured and the seeds thereof, which worth lakhs of rupees is fit for human consumption. A report on the de-seeded cardamom made by the Chief Government Analyst and Food Analyst reads as follows:- "As per the order WPC 25886/2017-IA No.2019 dated 25.11.2019 of Honourable High Court of Kerala, the Commissionerate of food safety constitute a committee for examination of cardamom which had kept sealed by Assistant Commissioner of food safety on 20.01.2016. The committee visited the Devaswom Board godown at Pamba on 03.12.2019 and collected the representative sample of "........" and deseed the "......." and collected 175 Specialty Indian Food Parks And Exports vs The Kerala State Co-Operative ... on 25 August, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135701108/ 3 gm of the seeds for analysis. The opinion of the analytical report of the food analyst is "The Said sample does not conform to the standards prescribed for cardamom seeds falling under Regulation 2.9.2.2 of food safety standards (food products standards & food additives) regulations 2011 (light seeds above the permissible limit) and is therefore substandard under Section 3(1)(zx) of food safety standard Act 2006." But the Honourable High Court asked whether the cardamom seeds is good for human consumption. In the light of the said report, the learned counsel for the petitioner Advocate Mathew John insisted that the petitioner may be permitted to extract seeds from the cardamom after husking and to sell the same. 11. The learned counsel for the 1st respondent stated that huge amounts are due to the 1 st respondent from the petitioner towards loss suffered by them consequent to the supply of substandard of cardamom by the petitioner. Therefore, the petitioner may not be permitted to take possession of the cardamom seeds and sell it. The 1 st respondent has a lien over the cardamom, which will remain in force till the petitioner makes good the loss caused to the 1st respondent, contended the counsel for the 1 st respondent. The learned Government Pleader submitted that the Food Safety Authority has initiated prosecution proceedings against the petitioner and any order that may be passed by this Court may not in any manner adversely affect the prosecution.
